children: By Mohi Narayan and Trixie Yap

Oil product inventories in Asia's fuel trading hub of Singapore lingered near three-week highs, government data showed on Thursday, as declines in light and middle distillate stocks were offset by an increase in residual fuels stocks.
Combined onshore inventories were at 39.04 million barrels in the week ended September 2, data from Enterprise Singapore showed, slightly below last week's 39.18 million barrels.
MIDDLE AND LIGHT DISTILLATE STOCKS FALL
Middle distillates stockpiles fell to a one-month low of slightly below 8 million barrels, despite a decline in net exports of diesel and jet fuel.
Diesel and gasoil net exports fell by 98% week on week, while jet fuel and kerosene net exports fell 12% over the same period.
For diesel and gasoil, imports grew significantly, reflecting the rise in cargo inflows from South Korea, China and Malaysia, in line with market expectations.
Exports of the transport and industrial fuel fell by almost 14% week on week, though volumes to South Africa surfaced as traders plugged the shortage there from the Middle East with Asian barrels.
On the jet fuel and kerosene front, net exports fell around 18% week on week, though imports from China resurfaced after a one-week hiatus.
Traders were expecting more arrivals from northeast Asia in the near term as refiners in the region ramp up their output.
Light distillate inventories, including naphtha and gasoline, fell to 10.68 million barrels in the week, the data showed.
Gasoline imports totalled about 249,000 metric tons (~2.1 million barrels) during the period, while exports reached roughly 463,000 tons.

Outbound gasoline volumes were led by Indonesia at about 178,000 tons, followed by Malaysia at around 101,000 tons. Gasoline inflows were led by India at nearly 109,000 tons, followed by China at about 70,000 tons.
Naphtha imports stood at about 385,000 tons (~3.5 million barrels), led by Russia at nearly 125,000 tons, followed by Algeria at around 62,000 tons.
Singapore exported about 128,000 tons of naphtha, with shipments to Taiwan at nearly 94,000 tons and Indonesia at around 30,000 tons, the data showed.
Residual fuel oil inventories increased for a third consecutive week, rising to the highest level since May 21 at 20.45 million barrels.
Total imports rose to about 931,000 tons in the week, with Brazil and South Korea emerging as the top suppliers.
Total exports fell to about 148,000 tons, with the majority heading to China.
